items.explanation: Dan accompanies a masculine singular noun; din accompanies a feminine singular noun. Learn the noun and its demonstrative together.

items.prompt: An injured person says: Għandi ___ miksura. (my foot)
items.explanation: Some body words take an attached possessive form. Ras becomes rasi, id becomes idi, and the paired eyes form becomes għajnejja. Do not append -i mechanically to every noun.

items.prompt: Two active girls join a team. Choose their adjective.
items.explanation: Do not use one adjective form for every subject. Compare sportiv / sportiva / sportivi and rqiq / rqiqa / rqaq. Some plural forms change inside the word.

items.prompt: Complete for one girl: Mila ___ n-netbol kull ġimgħa.
items.explanation: The subject controls the verb: jien nipprattika, hu jipprattika, aħna nipprattikaw and huma jipprattikaw. Keep the initial person marker and the plural ending together.

items.prompt: A meeting is in Ġunju. Which month is that?
items.explanation: Keep the weekday and month names distinct. L-Erbgħa is Wednesday, while Il-Ġimgħa is Friday. Jannar begins the year and Diċembru ends it.

items.prompt: A ticket shows 31. Write the standalone Maltese number.
items.explanation: For 21–29, put the unit before u għoxrin. Thirty is tletin; thirty-one is wieħed u tletin. This reference practises standalone number forms.

items.prompt: An event starts in the morning. Translate in the morning using one word.
